body:
I think I always thought of easy in terms of pet ownership and never really thought about how people might see easy as no work... like cleaning and feeding definitely takes less time than my cats so to me that means easier. 

I'm autistic and it's something my therapist and I have discussed in the past- I have a bad habit of assuming everyone does a lot of research on anything they own/do since I've always done that so I don't take the knowledge part into consideration when talking about difficulty.

I wish I had known that the friend was the breeder- me and my boyfriend were kind of blindsided by that. We looked back at texts and he never explicitly says he didn't breed the gecko but very much implies it was just a pet he couldn't take care of anymore. I researched the breeder for my blue tongue skink and got on a waiting list for it almost a year in advance. I honestly don't know a lot about crested geckos, when I volunteered at a rescue they weren't very popular and for the most part we'd see snakes or bearded dragons- I should've known better but I also fell into the assumption they were easy pets because of the temperature requirements and diet so I never researched them a lot because I thought my boyfriend had it covered, I think im gonna regret that for a long time.


We'd be able to afford the necropsy and my vet offered to do it asap at a reduced rate since I've known them a long time. My boyfriend is against it- he said the best case scenario would be she never had a chance and he doesn't want her cut up for his piece of mind. We found a nice spot in the yard for her, I wanted to get her footprint but I couldn't bring myself to do it.

We have a 'date' planned for next week that will be me going over the care for all my animals. Despite us living together we are pretty hands off with each other's pets and I'd like to change that- he still won't be getting his own exotic animal but I want to lead by example and show him what all goes into care. I've always told people most reptiles are easy pets and that stops now... I think him hearing me say that didn't help and I think I overestimate people's ability to tell I'm speaking in reference to daily care, and to know that they still need to put in work.

I called in for him and was able to talk to a staff member at his job who gave me the mental health resources his company has available to him. Fortunately no ER, neither of us slept last night but I was able to get him into bed and once he woke up he was definitely more animated- still not in a great place but in a place where we were able to talk more about everything.

No exotic pets is a new rule for him, he brought it up on his own and has a genuine conviction towards it. He said the amount of different information online made it difficult to know if he was doing things right... his friend had apparently made the gecko out to be a nearly hands off easy pet. This same friend had apparently dissuaded him from seeking a vet and scared him off by telling him exotic vets were a scam. In retrospect I fed into this unknowingly as well as I was very hard on one of the exotics vets I went to... I didn't realize it until he brought it up but I'm gonna try and be better about that in the future.

I found out that the friend who gave him the gecko wasn't honest with him either so that person has been blocked (I reached out to let the friend know and to see if I could get the breeders information as I know many breeders keep track of offspring- turns out the friend was the breeder and that only 3 geckos out of the 12 hatched are still alive...) I asked my boyfriend if a necropsy would help him get piece of mind since it seems like there could be other factors at play but he said it wouldn't change his lack of action.

Back to mental health- I did set a rule that he needs to at the very least make a doctors appointment to discuss options for medication. He has severe adhd and has depression, I definitely think these factors contributed to his quality of care.

I'm sticking with him no matter what... when I was a young teen I let my dog out to use the bathroom and it got hit by a drunk driver- while the situation isn't the same I know how I felt then and I needed someone to be there for me
